name: Harissa
subtitle: mutton pounded with rice into a smooth paste, eaten at dawn in a Srinagar winter

ingredients.note: cooked down with the meat until neither is distinguishable

prepNotes: Nothing to do with the North African chilli paste of the same name. This is a Kashmiri winter breakfast, sold from specialist shops that make nothing else.
It is pounded, not blended, for five or more hours until it is a smooth paste with no fibre left.

steps.text: Boil the mutton with the whole spices, fennel, dry ginger, salt and the water. Skim carefully.
Simmer 3 hours until the meat collapses at a touch. Fish out the whole spices.
Add the soaked rice and cook a further hour until it has disintegrated.
Now pound. Work it against the side of the pot with a heavy wooden spoon for at least an hour, until no fibre remains.
steps.tip: This is the dish. Blending gives you a puree, which is a different and lesser thing.

steps.text: Adjust with hot water to a thick, pourable paste and check the salt.
Serve in bowls with a ladle of smoking mustard oil and the crisp fried shallots over the top.
steps.tip: The hot oil poured over at the table is part of it.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and sets solid when cold. Reheat with hot water, stirring hard to bring it back. Freezes for a month.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
